page.name: Bring-your-own provider connections
page.h1: Connect the provider accounts you already pay for
page.metaTitle: BYOL connections — your own messaging accounts
page.metaDescription: Connect your own CPaaS or BSP accounts per channel, keep your contract and your pricing, and let the platform work above them.
page.lede: You keep the provider relationship you already have, connect it once, and the platform treats that account as a send path it can route through, pace against and read receipts from.

p: A connection holds the credentials for one provider account on one channel. An SMS connection, an email connection and a WhatsApp connection each carry their own credentials, their own limits and their own receipts — they are not one generic “channel” object with a type field.
bullets: SMS — the providers the console can connect today, each with the credential fields your provider actually requires
Email — your own sending account with that provider
WhatsApp — your own business account and its credentials

sections.h: Your contract, your pricing, your numbers
p: Because the account stays yours, so do the volume commitments, the rates and the sender identities attached to it. Nothing is repriced on the way through, and the connection never gives the platform control of your provider contract.
bullets: No markup on message credits — you pay your provider directly
Your existing sender numbers and registrations stay attached to your account
Disconnecting a provider leaves your account untouched

p: A connection gives the platform a send path, not control of your account. Registering a sender ID, raising a provider quota and approving a WhatsApp template are provider-side actions that stay with your team and the provider you already work with — which is also why they cannot be skipped by connecting here.

faq.q: Do I need to move my numbers or traffic to you?
faq.a: No. The accounts stay with your provider; the platform is given credentials so it can send through them and read status back.

faq.q: Can I connect more than one account on the same channel?
faq.a: Yes, and that is the point — multiple connected accounts on one channel are what makes routing and failover possible.

faq.q: What credentials does a connection need?
faq.a: Each provider lists the fields it requires, and the console only asks for those. Credential requirements per provider are documented in the integrations section.
